title: Prefetch Sentinel: Context-aware cache & batch recommendation narrative for Console
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a narrative-first Console panel called 'Prefetch Sentinel' that helps ops and platform engineers understand and apply cache/prefetch and batching recommendations. Unlike the existing recommendation cards, Prefetch Sentinel tells a short story for each suggestion: why the recommendation exists, estimated token savings and latency delta, confidence band based on recent traffic, and suggested rollout recipe (canary % + guardrail thresholds). It must include an isolated simulation preview (1-2 minute synthetic traffic), a toggleable guardrail quick-config (max latency increase, accuracy regression threshold), and a linkable audit record for compliance teams. The panel should be usable at the route/model level and aggregate to the project dashboard. This ticket covers final visual design, microcopy, accessibility checks, and a Figma prototype for design review and PM sign-off.
design_notes: Layout: left column is narrative header + aggregated KPIs (token burn delta, p90 latency drift, estimated monthly $), center is recommendation timeline with confidence bands and data sparklines, right column is quick-config card with guardrail toggles and rollout recipe builder. Components: Recommendation card (title, short rationale, impact bar, confidence strip), Simulation modal (choose workload sample, run 30s synthetic preview), Rollout recipe composer (canary percent slider with suggested presets: safe/medium/aggressive), Audit link (opens confluence PRD line-item). States: collapsed vs expanded recommendation, simulation in progress, validation error if guardrail thresholds conflict. Accessibility: all toggles keyboard-focusable, color contrast >= 4.5:1, labels for assistive tech. Tokens and microcopy: avoid jargon, show cost as both tokens and $ with hover breakdown. Data sources: runtime metrics + cost model from Optimize service. Margin notes: prefer progressive disclosure to avoid overwhelming early-stage users.
